context.body: I was glad when they said to me, “Let’s go to the LORD’s house!”.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

context.body: Royal, Poetic, and Prophetic Memory · Psalms 122:1–9
context.label: Canonical location

observations.body: The song rejoices in going to the LORD’s house, sees Jerusalem built compactly, names tribal ascent and David’s thrones, and prays for peace.
observations.label: Jerusalem, tribes, and David’s thrones: textual observation

observations.body: The passage keeps pilgrims, tribes, the house of David, friends, and the LORD, Jerusalem, gates, the LORD’s house, and thrones of judgment, rejoicing, standing, ascending, giving thanks, sitting in judgment, praying, and seeking good visible within David's story or later memory.
observations.label: Jerusalem, tribes, and David’s thrones: action, promise, or consequence

observations.body: pilgrims, tribes, the house of David, friends, and the LORD · Jerusalem, gates, the LORD’s house, and thrones of judgment · rejoicing, standing, ascending, giving thanks, sitting in judgment, praying, and seeking good · David’s house is located within pilgrimage, judgment, and Jerusalem’s peace
observations.label: Relationships named in Psalms 122:1–9

payload.posture: Read Psalms 122:1–9 as its own royal, poetic, and prophetic memory David setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The source places David’s house is located within pilgrimage, judgment, and Jerusalem’s peace inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
